title: NEET-UG 2026 Counselling: NRI and OCI Candidates Must Complete Document Verification
excerpt: The Medical Counselling Committee has directed NRI and OCI cardholders to verify their documents to confirm eligibility for the NEET-UG 2026 counselling process.
body:
• The Medical Counselling Committee has mandated that NRI and OCI candidates complete document verification to confirm their eligibility for NEET-UG 2026 counselling.
  • Candidates must submit proof of NRI or OCI status, including passport details, OCI card, and sponsor documentation, to participate in the counselling rounds.
  • The verification process is designed to prevent ineligible candidates from occupying seats reserved under the NRI quota at medical colleges across India.
  • Families in the diaspora should ensure all documents are current and properly authenticated before the verification deadline.

The Medical Counselling Committee has issued a directive requiring all NRI and Overseas Citizen of India cardholders who qualified in the NEET-UG 2026 examination to complete a mandatory document verification process before they can participate in the national counselling rounds for medical college admissions.

What NRI and OCI Candidates Need to Do

Under the MCC's guidelines, candidates seeking admission through the NRI quota must submit a set of documents verifying their eligibility. This includes valid passport copies, OCI card documentation, proof of the NRI sponsor's status — typically a parent or legal guardian residing abroad — and financial undertakings confirming the sponsor's ability to cover NRI-quota tuition fees, which are significantly higher than general category fees at most institutions.

The verification must be completed through the MCC's online portal within the stipulated timeframe. Candidates who fail to verify their documents by the deadline risk losing their eligibility for NRI-quota seats in the counselling rounds, with no provision for late submissions in most cases.

Why the Verification Matters

The document verification process serves as a gatekeeping mechanism to ensure that only genuinely eligible candidates occupy seats reserved under the NRI quota. In previous counselling cycles, complaints emerged about candidates claiming NRI status without valid documentation, or about sponsors whose NRI credentials had lapsed. The MCC's stricter verification protocol for 2026 appears designed to address these concerns.

"OCI and NRI candidates must verify documents for NRI eligibility."

— Medical Counselling Committee, NEET-UG 2026 directive

Medical colleges across India reserve a percentage of seats for NRI-sponsored candidates, with tuition fees for these seats typically ranging from several times to ten times the general category rate. The seats are highly sought after by diaspora families as a pathway for their children to obtain a medical degree in India.

Key Documents Required

Based on MCC guidelines for the counselling process, NRI and OCI candidates should have the following ready for verification:

Valid passport and visa documentation of the NRI sponsor, proof of residence abroad for the requisite period, the candidate's OCI card or valid Indian visa, NEET-UG 2026 scorecard and admit card, academic transcripts and mark sheets from qualifying examinations, a sponsorship affidavit notarized in the country of residence, and bank statements or financial documents demonstrating the sponsor's capacity to pay NRI-quota fees.

Practical Guidance for Diaspora Families

Families based in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and other countries with significant Indian diaspora populations should begin assembling documents immediately if they have not already done so. Authentication requirements vary — some documents may need apostille certification or attestation from the Indian embassy or consulate in the country of residence.

Candidates are advised to check the MCC website regularly for updates on counselling schedules, verification deadlines, and any changes to the document requirements. The MCC typically conducts multiple rounds of counselling, and NRI-quota seats that remain unfilled in earlier rounds may be converted to general seats in subsequent rounds.

For families navigating the process from abroad, ensuring that all documentation is complete, current, and properly authenticated well before the deadline is critical to avoiding last-minute complications that could jeopardize a seat.
